long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

I'm so excited to be bringing this workshop for the third time to Nelson this Sept 2026.

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)


Sunday 20th September - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2:00 - 4:00pm


Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.




Where: Founders Heritage Park, (St Peters Church) 87 Atawhai Dr, The Wood, Nelson. 7010 NEW ZEALAND
When: Sunday 20th Sept 2026
10:30am - 12:30pm or 2-4pm

long_description:
Overview

SEXY AGEING IS COMING TO STOKES VALLEY Have you noticed that training doesn't seem to work the same way it used to?

SEXY AGEING IS COMING TO STOKES VALLEY 🔥

Have you noticed that training doesn't seem to work the same way it used to?

Maybe the weight is slowly creeping up. Perhaps you're experiencing hot flushes, mood swings, poor sleep, brain fog, low energy, low sex drive or you're simply wondering why the things that once worked for your body no longer seem to work.

You're not alone.

So many women have been asking us for support and guidance to help them better understand what is happening to their bodies during perimenopause and menopause.

At Be Suite, we listened. That's why we are incredibly excited to welcome Tracy Minnoch-Nuku, founder and CEO of Sexy Ageing, to Stokes Valley.

Tracy has spent more than 30 years working within the health and fitness industry. Her career has included leadership roles with Fitness First Asia and Les Mills Asia Pacific, as well as co-founding one of Asia's first boutique fitness chains, Fire Fitness. As Tracy began experiencing menopause symptoms herself, she was shocked by the lack of evidence-based information and support available to women. Determined to change that, she founded Sexy Ageing, launched the internationally recognised podcast of the same name, wrote My Menopause Memoir, and created programmes specifically designed to help women thrive throughout this stage of life.This workshop will cover topics including:✔ Understanding perimenopause and menopause✔ Why your body changes as you age✔ Weight gain, sleep, mood, energy, and hormones✔ Training and nutrition strategies✔ Practical tools to help you feel stronger, healthier, and more confidentWhether you're experiencing symptoms yourself, preparing for the future, or supporting somebody you love, this workshop is for you.This event is open to both members and non-members, so bring your friends, mothers, sisters, daughters, workmates, and whānau.

Register your interest here and we'll be in touch with full registration details.

Because knowledge is power, and every woman deserves to understand her body.

Sue has graced the stage of New Zealand's 'Good Morning Show' multiple times, showcasing her vocal prowess and musical versatility. Additionally, Sue has lent her voice as a backup vocalist at the prestigious New Zealand Music Awards and has enjoyed significant success with her original country music in Australia.

Overview

Learn ways to resolve conflict with customers and co-workers, influence successful outcomes and develop a peaceful workplace.

Transform conflict and difficult situations, people/customers into opportunities by equipping your staff with the skills and techniques required to manage these situations with confidence, professionalism and pride.

We have all experienced the stress that comes from having unresolved conflicts with our customers and co-workers. Conflicts that are ignored or resolved poorly don’t go away, they cause people to feel resentful and to avoid each other. The effects on the business are a loss of productivity, turnover and absenteeism. Wherever two or more people come together, there is bound to be conflict. This workshop will give participants a six-step process that they can use and modify to resolve conflicts of any size. Participants will also learn crucial conflict resolution skills, including dealing with anger and using the Agreement Frame.


Learning Outcomes:

Transform conflict into opportunity
Develop constructive strategies for dealing with difficult behavior
Develop communication skills to diffuse the situation
Increase confidence and assertiveness in dealing with difficult behaviour
Manage your emotions and deal with stress
Understand the power of words and how to use them to your advantage


For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 06 354 5555

long_description:
Overview

Find inner stability in uncertain times through timeless Bhagavad Gita wisdom and practical tools for resilience, clarity and calm.

Inspire me workshops
Finding Ground in an Uncertain World; Ancient Wisdom for Modern Turbulence




The world feels increasingly chaotic—from economic pressure to global political shifts and an unpredictable future. When external conditions are completely out of our hands, how do we keep from feeling overwhelmed?
This interactive workshop bridges contemporary psychology with timeless philosophy from the Bhagavad Gita to help us build unshakeable internal resilience and stay anchored in times of uncertainty. We’ll look at the big picture, unpack what it means to live with the unknown, and share practical tools to maintain clarity amidst the noise.

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.

Meet your host Sivananda

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

The Future of Print — Panel Discussion-The Pit, Block 12, Massey University College of Creative Arts.
Wellington, Wellington-Event Brite
name: The Future of Print — Panel Discussion
venue:
The Pit, Block 12, Massey University College of Creative Arts.
Wellington, Wellington
long_description:
Overview

Hear from leading experts in typography and design history for a panel discussion on the Future of Print.

Join leading experts in typography, print culture, and design history, including Vanessa Wairata Edwards-Buerger, Professor Indra Kupferschmid, Kris Sowersby, and Professor Johnson Witehira, as they explore the past, present, and future of print.

Drawing on perspectives from Germany and Aotearoa New Zealand, the international panel will consider print's historical evolution, its complex and contested introduction to Aotearoa, and the current and future roles of printing in visual and material culture.

Tuesday 8 September

5.30 – 8.00 pm

Panel Discussion 6.15 pm

The Pit Lecture Theatre, Block 12 Level C

Massey University Pukeahu Wellington Campus

Light refreshments will be served from 5.30pm, before the panel discussion begins at 6.15 pm. Parking on campus will be free in unmarked, unlined car parks.

Vanessa Wairata Edwards-Buerger (Ngāti Tūwharetoa, Whakatohea, Ngāti Kuri & Ngāti Kahu) is an artist and curator based in Whanganui, where she works as Educator at Te Whare o Rehua Sarjeant Gallery. Her print practice explores Māori cultural sovereignty, whakapapa, and storytelling through traditional and experimental techniques like drypoint, relief printing, and mixed-media sgraffito. She is a founding member of Toi Whakaata Māori, a collective of Māori printmakers dedicated to advancing Māori printmaking through creative practice, collaboration, and cultural exchange.

Professor Indra Kupferschmid is Professor of Typography and Type Design at HBKsaar (University of the Arts Saarbrücken, Germany) and a member of the DIN committees on type legibility and classification. An internationally respected typographic scholar, her research has focused on the history of twentieth-century German sans-serif typefaces, including Akzidenz-Grotesk and Neue Haas-Grotesk/Helvetica, as well as the ways in which type production technologies have evolved over time. Author of the award-winning typographic reference Buchstaben kommen selten allein and co-author of Helvetica Forever, she has spent nearly three decades teaching typography across Europe. For more information: https://www.hbksaar.de/personen/details/kupferschmid

Kris Sowersby is the founder, director & lead type designer of Klim Type Foundry (Klim). Through Klim, Sowersby has developed bespoke typographic solutions for a global clientele, including The Financial Times, PayPal, and National Geographic and Apple. Within Aotearoa, his practice includes the creation of custom type for The Bank of New Zealand, Trade Me, and Tourism New Zealand. He is a member of the Alliance Graphique Internationale and was named an Art Laureate by The Arts Foundation for his continuing contribution to New Zealand Art and Design. For more information: https://klim.co.nz/about/

Professor Johnson Witehira (Tamahaki, Ngāi Tū-te-auru & Ngāti Hinekura) is Professor of Toi Hangarau – Creative Technologies – at Massey University, and Head of School of Te Rewa o Puanga, Music and Screen Arts. He is a distinguished indigenous artist, designer, and academic whose work integrates Mātauranga Māori with contemporary creative technologies, aiming to decolonize and indigenize design and digital media. Together with Kris Sowersby, Professor Witehira developed Matarongo, a contemporary digital typeface family built from rigorous research into Māori letterforms. Witehira traced Māori letterforms through traditional crafts, from tuhi waitohu (hand lettering) to tātai kupu toi (typography), and Sowersby translated that research into type. For more information: https://www.johnsonwitehira.studio/about

The Future of Print is presented by Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, Massey University, in partnership with The German Embassy Wellington.

Nelson, Nelson Region-Event Brite
name: Friendship and Networking For Creatives
venue:
Project 100
Nelson, Nelson Region
long_description:
Overview

A warm, fun workshop about networking and friendship for writers, artists and anyone wanting to connect to a community.

In a world where being a part of a community is more important than ever in career and life--especially in creative industries--we’re faced with the challenge of how to make long lasting, vital connections.

When we’re younger, society is set up to help us make friends and to build professional connections, whether it be through school, university or sporting or social groups.

But what if we don’t feel comfortable in those settings?

Or what if we’re older and have experienced some of the ups and down that life can bring, leaving us with a feeling of isolation.

Or what if we’re wanting to make connections that would help us in our careers but aren’t quite sure how to go about it?

Join psychotherapist Emma Constantine and author, poet and world traveller George Penney in this two hour talk that covers practical steps on network building and friendship for creative people wanting to broaden their social and professional lives.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

Are you a woman in business looking for a supportive community to help you connect, grow, and learn?
As an Inner Circle member, you can attend as many of our networking hubs as you like for FREE!
Empower Her is a global female networking community, that offers a welcoming and safe environment for women of all business backgrounds and experiences.
Empower Her provides a safe space where you can share your business with others, connect with like-minded women in business, and prioritise collaboration over competition.
By joining Empower Her, you will not only expand your professional network but also gain access to a supportive community of like-minded individuals who are committed to helping each other succeed.Find out more about us and check up our upcoming events on our website.
